newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 31.

text.p: General Electric Co and Pratt & Whitney plan to expand their jet-engine venture to work on a proposed Airbus jet, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.
- Safeway Inc made a $1.65 billion stock bid for the 65 percent of Vons Cos Inc that it does not already own.
- Bethlehem Steel Corp plans a $375 million restructuring charge for the proposed sale of four unprofitable operations.
- Texaco Inc will set decision-making along business lines rather than geographical ones.
- Strikes at two General Motors Corp plants have forced the company to shut down some truck plants.
- The U.S. gross domestic product aPLGDP fell to a 2.2 percent annual rate during the third quarter against a 4.7 percent rate in the second quarter.
- CompUSA Inc reported strong quartertly earnings.
- B.A.T Industries Plc reported a 5.0-percent greater quarterly pre-tax profit on solid growth in cigarette sales.
- Four large paper companies signed a forestry agreement with New Hampshire and an environmental group to manage private timberlands.
- Chip sales are expected to grow 3.5 percent in the fourth quarter.
- Mexico's peso closed at a record low of eight pesos to the U.S. dollar.
- TWA's flight-attendants union filed a suit against its president and a machinists union for supposedly planning a hostile organizing raid.
- Vanguard Group surpassed Fidelity as the fund family that is bringing in the most money this year.
- The U.S. bond market closed lower after homes sales figures came out. The market is now waiting for more economic indicators to be released on Friday.
- Shares of Burlington Northern Santa Fe have been falling on the stock market because investors expect it to make a bid for Conrail Inc.
